title: The Effects of Interrupting Periods of Prolonged Sitting by Acute Physical Activity with Different Densities on Cognitive Outcomes: A Randomized-Crossover Trial in University Students
summary:
This study investigates whether different ways of interrupting long periods of sitting with short periods of moderate physical activity can influence thinking and memory performance in university students. Long periods of uninterrupted sitting are common in everyday life, but it is not yet clear whether the timing of physical activity breaks affects thinking and memory.

The study aims to determine whether different patterns of physical activity breaks during a prolonged sitting period lead to differences in cognitive performance and in changes in a naturally occurring substance in the blood that is involved in the functioning of brain cells.

The study is conducted as a randomized cross-over study. Each participant attends four study visits. During the first visit, sociodemographic information such as age and sex, body measurements, physical fitness, usual physical activity and sedentary behaviour, sleep duration, and other relevant health information are collected. Participants also become familiar with the cognitive tests. During the following three visits, participants complete three different conditions in a random order: one condition with uninterrupted sitting while watching a 90-minute documentary, and two conditions in which the 90-minute sitting period is interrupted by three 5-minute periods of moderate cycling, with different intervals between the activity breaks. Thinking and memory performance and blood samples are collected before and after each condition. Participants also complete short questionnaires about their usual physical activity, motivation, concentration, mental fatigue, and sleepiness

interventions.name:
Low-Density Physical Activity

Participants will watch a non-arousing documentary for 90 minutes while seated. The sitting period will be interrupted by three 5-minute bouts of cycling on a cycle ergometer at moderate intensity. The cycling bouts will take place at approximately 20, 50, and 80 min

High-Density Physical Activity

Participants will watch a non-arousing documentary for 90 minutes while seated. The sitting period will be interrupted by three 5-minute bouts of cycling on a cycle ergometer at moderate intensity. The cycling bouts will take place at approximately 50, 65, and 80 mi

Passive Control

Participants will remain seated for 90 minutes while watching a non-arousing documentary. No physical activity breaks will be performed during the 90-minute sitting period.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants must meet all of the following inclusion criteria: (1) young adults aged 18 to 30 years; (2) absence of acute and chronic diseases or health conditions that could interfere with study participation; and (3) low risk of adverse health effects in response to physical activity, assessed through a personal interview and established screening questionnaires, including the Physical Activity Readiness Questionnaire and the Beck Depression Inventory-II.
Exclusion criteria:
Participants will be excluded if they are outside the age range of 18 to 30 years or if any of the following criteria apply: neurological disorders (e.g., epilepsy or multiple sclerosis); psychiatric disorders (e.g., schizophrenia, manifest depression, or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder); orthopedic disorders (e.g., symptomatic disc herniation); cardiovascular disorders (e.g., severe heart failure, pacemaker, or heart valve disease); severe endocrine disorders (e.g., manifest thyroid dysfunction, obesity with a body mass index >30, or insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes mellitus); muscular or tendon disorders (e.g., myositis or tendovaginitis); visual disorders (e.g., uncorrected visual impairment or known color vision deficiency); acute injuries or surgery within the previous 6 months; acute use of legal or illegal intoxicating substances; or pregnancy. A score >13 on the Beck Depression Inventory-II or a score ≥14 on the Adult Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Self-Report Screening Scale constitutes an exclusion criterion.
